topic: TSMC's 'previous definition' size of the 2023 foundry industry
disagreement: TSMC's 2Q24 call gives US$115bn for 2023 under the previous definition; its 2024 annual report gives US$150bn for the same quantity; its 2023 annual report gave US$114bn for the 2023 foundry segment.
possible_reasons: typographical error in the 2024 annual report
different 'previous definition' (e.g. incl. IDM foundry units) in the annual report
rationale: US$115bn matches TSMC's own 2023 report (US$114bn) and the Foundry 2.0 share arithmetic; US$150bn has no supporting figure elsewhere.
remaining_uncertainty: TSMC has not explained the US$150bn figure; a check of the Chinese-language 2024 annual report could settle whether it is a typo.

disagreement: TSMC puts Foundry 2.0 at US$305bn with TSMC at 40%; Counterpoint puts it at US$320bn with TSMC at 38%; both say +16%.
possible_reasons: Counterpoint adds photomask suppliers and 'others' differently
different company lists for non-memory IDMs and OSATs
TSMC counts its own consolidated revenue; Counterpoint may use a different TSMC figure
rationale: Same concept, different proprietary scopes; neither publishes its company list. The ~5% gap is within definitional noise.
remaining_uncertainty: Neither firm discloses the population or double-count treatment.

disagreement: TrendForce projected China's 2027 mature-process capacity share at 33% (Oct 2023) and 39% (Dec 2023), and separately Chinese foundries' share of top-10 mature capacity at >25% by end-2025.
possible_reasons: different node cut-off (>28nm vs 28nm and older)
different population (all fabs vs foundries vs top-10 foundries)
rationale: The releases do not state their populations; the >25% figure is explicitly top-10-only, so not comparable with the other two.
remaining_uncertainty: Which population (foundry vs all fabs incl. IDMs) each TrendForce figure uses; SEMI World Fab Forecast could give an independent check (RU-0052).

disagreement: 2023 foundry revenue is US$111.5bn (TrendForce top 10), US$114bn (TSMC) or US$124.0bn (TechInsights).
possible_reasons: TrendForce counts only top 10 (95% of market)
TechInsights includes IDMs providing foundry services
TechInsights later revised its 2023 decline from 13% to 14%
rationale: Gaps track scope: top-10-only < whole pure-foundry < incl. IDM foundry services.
remaining_uncertainty: TechInsights' inclusion list for IDM foundry services (e.g. Intel internal) is paywalled.

topic: TSMC and Samsung shares of the pure-foundry market, 2Q26
disagreement: TrendForce: TSMC 72.5%, Samsung 5.9%; Counterpoint: TSMC 73%, Samsung 7%.
possible_reasons: Counterpoint includes Samsung's foundry service for internal System LSI chips; TrendForce counts the foundry business only
rationale: Both are consistent once Samsung's captive revenue treatment is accounted for.
remaining_uncertainty: Samsung does not disclose Foundry revenue or its internal share.
